# HAProxy (HTTPS) — root-context-sse

App at /, HAProxy terminates TLS on https://localhost:9443/ and forwards over plain HTTP, PUSH over Server-Sent Events. SERVER_FORWARD_HEADERS_STRATEGY=NATIVE so the push URL is built with the https scheme and the browser does not block the event stream as mixed content.

Proxy URL on `https://localhost:9443`: `/`

## Configuration

See [docker-compose.yml](./docker-compose.yml) for service definitions.

HAProxy config (`haproxy/https/root-context-sse/vaadin.cfg`), mounted as
`conf.d/10-vaadin.cfg`:

```haproxy
# App at /, HAProxy terminates TLS on https://localhost:9443/ and forwards over
# plain HTTP, PUSH over Server-Sent Events.
#
# As in https/root-context there is no X-Forwarded-Proto rule: the shared base
# derives it from the bind's TLS state, so the push URL is built with the https
# scheme and the browser does not block the event stream as mixed content.
frontend vaadin-in from vaadin-front
    bind :443 ssl crt /usr/local/etc/haproxy/tls/localhost.crt

    # HAProxy relays an upgrade with no configuration at all and has no keyword
    # to stop it, so the refusal is written out. The 501 comes from the proxy
    # rather than from Atmosphere.
    http-request deny deny_status 501 if { req.hdr(Upgrade) -m found }

    default_backend vaadin-app

backend vaadin-app from vaadin
    server vaadin vaadin:8080
```

The `global` section, and the two `defaults` sections this file
inherits from, come from the shared
[haproxy-base.cfg](../../haproxy-base.cfg), mounted read-only beside
it as `conf.d/00-base.cfg`. Base and scenario only parse as a pair.
